extracted.title: How Bad Can It Git? Characterizing Secret Leakage in Public GitHub Repositories
extracted.venue: NDSS Symposium 2019 (peer reviewed); copy read from the symposium's site
extracted.inclusion: included (Part A), a judgement for review: the measure is the repository owner's removal of a leaked secret (taking content down); the outcome is how long secrets stayed exposed and whether removal ended exposure; method stated. The paper does not measure providers' revocation (the gate's recollection confirmed)
extracted.population: secrets found through GitHub's Search API and monitored from 4 April 2018 (count not stated in the section read); collection ran 31 October 2017 to 20 April 2018
extracted.data_public: inputs public (GitHub Search API, BigQuery public snapshot); derived data not stated
outcome_facts: "about 6% of all detected secrets were removed" in the first hour; "at the end of the first day, over 12% of secrets were gone, while only 19% were gone after 16 days"; "81% of the secrets we discover were not removed" (Section V-E)
"none of the monitored repos had their history rewritten, meaning the secrets were trivially accessible via Git history" (Section V-E)
